text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.

LONDON - UK shares fell for the first time in three sessions as worries over rising interest rates resurfaced after yesterday's UK budget and Wall Street suffered a bout of jitters after its recent record-breaking run. The FTSE 100 index closed down 19.2 points at 4,049.2.

FRANKFURT - German shares ended bourse dealings lower, off record highs after weakness on foreign markets, but supported by strength in German bond market. The 30-share DAX closed bourse down 13.61 points to 2,797.03. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 2,793.86.

PARIS - French shares closed slightly down on prolonged profit-taking and a lower Wall Street after two stronger-than-expected U.S. economic reports. The French truckers' strike is worrying mainly foreign investments but negotiations resumed in the afternoon between striking French truck drivers and employers and ministers expressed optimism that an agreement in the 10-day-old dispute that has choked French highways could be reached within hours. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 4.31 points or 0.19 percent to 2,270.77.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended near the day's lows in line with most European markets in the wake of stronger-than-expected data U.S. economic data, a sagging Wall Street and easing SMI futures. The All-share SPI index ended 16.18 points lower at 2,460.78.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended on a feeble tone, due mostly to profit-taking after the Nikkei average had risen for three straight sessions, the impact of the Bank of Japan's "tankan" business sentiment survey released in the morning was limited. The Nikkei 225 ended down 72.97 points or 0.34 percent to 21,345.28.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks leaped to an all-time high and record close, overcoming earlier weakness on futures-related activity and buying in favoured property developers. The Hang Seng index rose 45.62 points to close at 13,530.95.
SYDNEY - Australian shares closed weaker but were lifted off the midsession lows by bargain hunting in the afternoon session. By the close, the All Ordinaries index lost 5.3 points to 2,376.7.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended mixed after 27 minutes of trade due to an electronic trading system failure, Industrials were firm, lifted by a stronger rand, while golds fell on an ailing bullion price. The system was halted twice, in the morning and in the afternoon, due to its inadequate performance on dealers systems, the Johannesburg Stock Exchange said. The Industrial index ended up 36 points to 8,051.4, the Gold index was down 9.7 points to 1,563.7 and the All-share index added 28.6 points to 6,749.9.
